title: Morphisms and generic modifications of multipointed curves
statement: Let $T,E$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $e:E\to T$, and let $P=(X_P,D_P)$, $Q=(X_Q,D_Q)$ be multipointed $T$-curves [def-trf-multipointed-curve]. A morphism of pairs $f:P\to Q$ is a pair of $T$-morphisms $f_X:X_P\to X_Q$ and $f_D:D_P\to D_Q$ commuting with the marking immersions. Its curve and marking maps after any base change are the canonical pullback maps [def-pc-base-change]; the base-changed marking inclusion is likewise the canonical pullback of the marking. Say that $f$ is an $e$-modification if both maps are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], each restricts to an isomorphism over some open of its target whose inclusion and inverse-image inclusion both induce injective maps on sections over every open, and both maps become isomorphisms after base change along $e$. Thus the two isomorphism opens are schematically dense, with no quasi-compactness assumption on the opens. For an integral base [def-pc-integral-scheme], taking $e$ to be the inclusion of its generic point [def-sc-generic-point] gives an $\eta$-modification.

source.place: Temkin, Stable modification of relative curves, §1.2 (multipointed curves, modifications and stability); §3.1 (generic modifications)
